page: Amazon Web Services t3a.medium is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The instance provisions two vCPUs across one physical core using simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity is set to 4.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included, and the instance provides no local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. The network interface reflects a 0 Gbps baseline bandwidth configuration.

Benchmark evaluations position the t3a.medium primarily in entry-tier performance brackets due to its shared and burstable resource allocation. Synthetic compute testing records a PassMark CPU score of 1849.5 and Geekbench scores of 681.0 in single-core and 920.0 in multi-core execution. PassMark encryption performance reaches 1616.07, supported by integrated AES and SHA instruction sets. Memory testing demonstrates cached read bandwidth of 77.52 GB/sec for 16 KB blocks and uncached large-block read throughput of 20.08 GB/sec. Application tests register 1.26 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.53 GB/sec throughput for static web delivery.

Given its burstable CPU credit architecture and low baseline computing capacity, the instance offers strong cost efficiency for variable or intermittent usage patterns where continuous compute is unnecessary. It is poorly suited for sustained multi-threaded computing, heavy data ingestion, or demanding database operations due to low multi-core margins and lack of local NVMe storage. Workloads aligned with this hardware profile include development environments, microservices, low-traffic web applications, and periodic background tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services t3a.medium is a burstable general-purpose instance featuring an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz. The instance allocates 2 vCPUs from a single physical core along with 4.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz. It contains no dedicated GPU hardware and includes no local instance storage, operating entirely with remote block storage under the AWS Nitro System. Across synthetic and operational benchmarks, the instance delivers entry-level compute output, scoring 681.0 in Geekbench single-core, 920.0 in multi-core, and achieving 1.26 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. Static web serving throughput measures 1.53 GB/sec. Because compute capacity follows a burstable model, the t3a.medium provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads with low average CPU utilization, making it suited for lightweight web applications, code testing environments, staging servers, and intermittent background services.
